summary.headline: A debt-light, cash-rich supplier to its parent, but the price is about 30% above fair value
summary.text: ACL Plastics PLC (APLA.N0000) makes the PVC compound that coats cables and sells almost all of it to its parent ACL Cables (65.2%) and sister company Kelani Cables. It had a record 2025/26 (revenue +17% to Rs 2.85bn, profit +72% to Rs 798mn, ROE 20%), and the six months to September 2026 were up again (revenue +16%, EPS Rs 10.72 against Rs 8.37). But the September quarter's gross margin fell to 24.9% from 31.3%, quarterly profit slipped 10%, and stock and money owed by the group jumped, so operating cash was −Rs 456mn in the half and the company borrowed Rs 221mn for the first time in years. Over half the equity (Rs 2.5bn, Rs 59.86 a share) sits in unit trusts, deposits and listed shares, which also supply a quarter to a third of profit. With the shared CAPM method the required return is 18.3% (beta 0.98), higher than the 16.5% used before, and the methods put fair value at about Rs 120 (was Rs 139). At Rs 156.25 the share is about 30% above it. Still a good business on the four tests (watch list), but I'd buy only at up to about Rs 102 and treat under Rs 90 as a strong buy.

quality.reason: High returns, no real debt, no loss in ten years and profit mostly turned into cash, but it depends on two group customers and half its equity is treasury investments.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
tests.note: Twelve months to September 2026 (code-calculated); 19.8% in 2025/26; five-year average about 22% (37%, 25%, 15%, 13%, 20%), despite carrying Rs 2.5bn of unit trusts and deposits.

tests.label: Net debt no more than equity
tests.note: Rs 200mn short-term loan and Rs 21mn overdraft at September 2026 against Rs 14mn of cash, but Rs 2.4bn of unit trusts and deposits; no borrowings at March 2025 or 2026.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: Profit fell 34% in 2023/24 (actually 28% on PBT) and swings with PVC margins; unit-trust and exchange gains were Rs 187mn of 2025/26's Rs 1,110mn profit before tax.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Operating cash Rs 1.15bn (2024/25) and Rs 0.50bn (2025/26) against profit of Rs 1.26bn, but −Rs 456mn in April–September 2026 as stock rose Rs 367mn and receivables Rs 296mn. Watch: a second weak half would fail this test.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of four methods 30/50/20 (Rs 89.46 / 120.39 / 163.66), giving Rs 119.77 (1.07x NAV). The methods are a DCF of the PVC business plus treasury investments, justified P/E, justified P/B and residual income, all from scripts/valuation.py at an 18.3% cost of equity (WACC 18.0%).

highlights.title: Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited)

highlights.title: A softer September quarter
highlights.text: Revenue rose 28% to Rs 788mn, but the gross margin fell to 24.9% from 31.3%, so profit slipped 10% to Rs 157mn (EPS Rs 3.73 against Rs 4.13); the exchange line turned to a Rs 19mn loss.

highlights.title: Cash went the other way
highlights.text: Stock rose to Rs 973mn from Rs 606mn and receivables (mostly the two group customers) to Rs 1.28bn from Rs 0.99bn. Operating cash was −Rs 456mn, so it withdrew Rs 285mn from unit trusts and took a Rs 200mn short-term loan plus a Rs 21mn overdraft.

highlights.title: Record 2025/26
highlights.text: Revenue +17% to Rs 2.85bn, gross margin 31% (24%), profit +72% to Rs 798mn, EPS Rs 18.94; capex Rs 53mn (machinery, equipment and a vehicle). Dividend Rs 3.75 a share (Rs 158mn) paid in September 2026.

highlights.title: Two customers, both in the family
highlights.text: Sales to ACL Cables (Rs 1.62bn) and Kelani Cables (Rs 1.64bn) including taxes exceed the Rs 2.85bn of revenue excluding taxes, so essentially all sales go to the group, at board-approved price lists; they owed Rs 815mn at March 2026, and ACL Cables a further Rs 114mn loan.

methodReadings.reading: The price is 1.4x NAV; Rs 59.86 of it is unit trusts, deposits and listed shares.
Good, and higher on the PVC business alone (about 28% on operating capital), because half the equity earns treasury returns.
Low on paper, but justified P/E at an 18.3% required return is only about 5.4x on base-case EPS.
The PVC business is worth Rs 63–117 a share at 16.6–19.5% WACC; add Rs 59.86 of investments.
Rs 3.75 for 2025/26, about 20% of profit; cover is ample but cash flow was negative in H1.
Volumes and prices are set by ACL Cables and Kelani Cables.

models.name: DCF of the PVC business (WACC, less net debt) + treasury investments
models.comment: The PVC business (gross profit less administrative costs, after the 28.1% tax rate): after-tax profit Rs 0.549bn (Sep 2026 quarter × 4) / Rs 0.621bn (2025/26) / Rs 0.658bn (twelve months), growing 3% / 5.5% / 6.5% for five years then 4% / 4.5% / 5%, reinvesting growth ÷ 20% / 25% / 30% return on new capital, discounted at WACC 19.5% / 18.0% / 16.6%, less net debt Rs 0.21bn (Rs 63 / 90 / 117 a share), plus Rs 59.86 a share of unit trusts, deposits and listed shares at book. 48–61% of the DCF value comes after year five.

models.name: P/E method (justified P/E)
models.comment: EPS to March 2027 of Rs 17.70 / 19.20 / 21.20 × justified P/E of 4.6 / 5.4 / 6.5 (from long-run ROE 15% / 18% / 21%, growth 4% / 4.5% / 5% and the cost of equity). Base is 9.8% below the Rs 21.29 run-rate because the September quarter's margin fell to 24.9% and EPS to Rs 3.73.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: NAV Rs 111.51 × (long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 15% / 18% / 21%, cost of equity 19.8% / 18.3% / 16.8%.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Book Rs 111.51, ROE moving from 20.7% to 15% / 18% / 21% over 10 years, 20% payout, then growth 4% / 4.5% / 5%, at a 19.8% / 18.3% / 16.8% cost of equity.

modelsNote: All four methods come from scripts/valuation.py and are weighted equally. Growth check: assumed 3% / 5.5% / 6.5% against 4.8% supported (reinvestment rate 24.4% × return on capital 19.9% in 2025/26), all within 2 points. The DCF values the PVC business only and adds the treasury investments, because their gains sit in operating profit in the annual report but in finance income in the interims. Dividend model left out: at a 20% payout its value would rest on the payout assumed after year five. Cost of debt is the bond yield (no borrowings at either year end); debt weight only 3%.

scenarios.common: 10-year rupee bond 12.24%, risk-free rate 8.24%, beta 0.98. Unit trusts, deposits and listed shares Rs 2.52bn (Rs 59.86 a share) and borrowings Rs 0.22bn at September 2026. Maintenance capex about depreciation (Rs 16–27mn). Payout 20%.

sensitivity.title: Justified price to book, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Growth 4.5%. Today's Rs 156.25 needs ROE to settle near 21% with a 16.8% cost of equity.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 48,080 in total, against Rs 78,125 at Rs 156.25.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 101.80 needs a 35% fall. The share hasn't traded that low since the December 2025 subdivision (low Rs 115.25 in 2025/26, Rs 135 in July–September 2026), so the buy price is unlikely to be reached without a broad market fall or a clear profit setback.

higher: Gross margin back above 30% in the December 2026 quarter.
Stock and group receivables falling back and the Rs 221mn of borrowing repaid.
A bigger or special dividend from the Rs 2.5bn of investments.
Real sales outside the group (plumbing, agriculture, telecom products) showing up in the figures.
lower: A second quarter of margins near 25%, or the group squeezing prices (it buys essentially all output).
Operating cash staying negative as the parent pays more slowly.
PVC resin prices or the rupee moving against it.
The investments being lent to or used for group companies on poor terms.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the annual report to March 2026 and the interim report to September 2026. Per-share figures before the December 2025 1-for-10 subdivision are as printed unless marked. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

fullText:
Summary: ACL Plastics PLC (APLA.N0000) makes the PVC compound that coats cables, and sells about 97% of it to its parent ACL Cables and sister company Kelani Cables. It is a small, debt-free and very profitable business: return on equity was 20% in the year to March 2026 and has averaged about 22% over five years, and about a third of its value is cash and unit trusts (Rs 2.2bn net, about Rs 52 a share). Profit for the six months to September 2026 rose 28% (EPS Rs 10.72), though the September quarter was 10% lower as margins narrowed. At Rs 159 (30 September close; check the live price) the share trades at 7.5x trailing earnings and 1.4x its NAV of Rs 111.51. The methods put fair value at about Rs 139, so the price is about 14% above it: fairly priced rather than cheap. I'd buy at up to about Rs 118 and treat under Rs 104 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 159.00 (closing price 30 September 2026, from the interim report). Please check it live. In July–September 2026 it traded between Rs 135 and Rs 172. It closed March 2026 at Rs 131.25.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 1.53bn (up 16%), profit Rs 452mn (up 28%), EPS Rs 10.72 (Rs 8.37). The September quarter: revenue Rs 788mn (up 28%), gross margin 25% (31%), profit Rs 157mn (down 10%), EPS Rs 3.73.
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 2.85bn (up 17%), gross margin 31% (24%), profit Rs 798mn (up 72%), EPS Rs 18.94 (Rs 11.03), ROE 20%. Trailing EPS is about Rs 21.29.
NAV Rs 111.51 a share (September 2026). 42.1 million shares after the 1-for-10 split. ACL Cables owns 65%.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Justified P/B | 65.0 | 117.1 | 195.1 | 117.1
Business at a P/E plus cash | 109.5 | 161.3 | 220.9 | 157.7
Residual income | 68.5 | 133.4 | 271.6 | 141.6
Average | 81.0 | 137.3 | 229.2 | 138.8
Fair value about Rs 139 (30% bear, 50% base, 20% bull). Buy at up to Rs 118 (15% below); strong buy under Rs 104 (25% below).

Assumptions
Cost of equity 18% / 16.5% / 15%, against government bonds of about 12%. Long-run ROE 13% / 17% / 21% (five-year average about 22%). Growth 6% / 6.5% / 7%. Operating business: profit after tax of Rs 9.10 / 13.30 / 16.60 a share at 6 / 8 / 10 times, plus Rs 54.90 of net cash and investments.

What stands out
- Debt-free with Rs 2.4bn of unit trusts, deposits and cash (Rs 221mn of short-term borrowing at September).
- Captive customers: 97% of sales to ACL Cables and Kelani Cables. This keeps volumes steady but means the group sets the margin.
- Some of the latest profit is market and currency gains (Rs 77mn unit trusts, Rs 66mn exchange in the half).
- Dividend raised to Rs 3.75 (from Rs 2.50), about 20% of profit.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 139, 150 up to Rs 118, 150 up to Rs 104: average about Rs 122, about Rs 61,100 in total. Rs 118 needs about a 26% fall; the share was Rs 131 in March 2026, so that's within reach in a market dip.

What would change my view
Higher: strong cable demand at ACL and Kelani, gross margin back above 30%, a bigger or special dividend, customers outside the group.
Lower: the group squeezing margins, PVC resin costs rising, a cable slowdown, the cash being used on poor terms within the group.

Business tests: 4 of 4 passed, so it's a good business priced a little above fair value: watch list.

management.takeaway: Management promises to protect margins and to sell beyond the group's cable makers, but the first half of 2026/27 brought a lower margin, negative operating cash and new short-term borrowing.

said.text: 2025/26 was the best year in the company's history: revenue +17% to Rs 2,851mn, profit +72% to Rs 798mn
Demand came from ACL Cables and Kelani Cables and a construction sector that grew about 12%, plus higher CEB infrastructure spending
Gross margin rose to 31% from 24% despite lower selling prices, through cost control and efficiency
Plants ran at peak efficiency; capacity utilisation 91% on output of 6,266 tonnes
Rising raw material prices, rupee weakness and global trade shifts are the risks for 2026/27

plans.text: Grow new product lines for plumbing, agriculture, telecom infrastructure and construction, to become a broad plastics supplier rather than a cable-only one
Reduce dependence on any single customer or end market
Protect margins while investing in technology, people and sustainable manufacturing
Expand recycling of production waste and PVC scrap, and explore take-back of end-of-life plastics

investing.text: Capex booked in 2025/26 (machinery Rs 16.5mn, equipment Rs 9.2mn, a vehicle Rs 26.5mn)
Machinery and equipment with soundproofing and recycling capability
No material capital commitments at March 2026; Rs 83.8mn of letters of credit for materials
Dividend of Rs 3.75 a share for 2025/26, paid September 2026
Surplus cash kept in unit trusts (mainly Capital Alliance) and deposits

track.promise: Keep growing with the cable and construction recovery
track.result: Revenue +16% in April–September 2026 (Rs 1,526mn) and +28% in the September quarter (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 2)
September quarter gross margin 24.9% against 31.3% a year earlier; 29.3% for the half against 29.6% (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 2)

track.promise: Disciplined working capital and strong cash generation
track.result: Operating cash −Rs 456mn in the half as stock rose to Rs 973mn (Rs 606mn) and receivables to Rs 1,282mn (Rs 986mn); Rs 221mn borrowed (Interim, pp. 4, 6)

track.promise: Sell beyond the group to cut customer concentration
track.result: No split in the interim; in 2025/26 group sales including taxes (Rs 3.25bn) still exceeded revenue excluding taxes (Rs 2.85bn) (p. 141)
Rs 3.75 a share (Rs 158mn) paid on 2 September 2026, against Rs 105mn a year earlier (Interim, p. 7)
